sentences.text: Roseburia inulinivorans is a strictly anaerobic, slightly curved rod obtained from human stools, with type strain A2-194 (DSM 16841).
It is a polysaccharide-utilizing bacterium of the human colon that produces butyric acid when grown on glucose, starch or inulin.
On the host-derived sugar fucose it instead forms propionate and propanol, and the propanediol pathway for propionate production occurs in this species.
Long-chain inulin was reported to be used for growth by Roseburia inulinivorans but by none of the bifidobacteria tested.
A study reported it among butyrate-producing species reduced in Crohn's disease patients, and another reported it more abundant at baseline in Crohn's patients who later achieved remission.
